## Actualizacion acotada — sombras 3D (issue 203, 2026-10-20)

These facts supersede the affected older measurements below; this is not a full
environment re-exploration. Checkout version is 0.30.1; npm state was not queried.
No limits, generation policies, dependencies or release settings changed.

## Stack
TypeScript (tsc 7.x) end to end. pnpm monorepo (`pnpm@11.4.0`, 16 workspace projects: the root plus 11 under `packages/` and 4 under `examples/`): `packages/engine` (ECS-style entities/components, fixed-step simulation, scene lifecycle, collisions/physics, state machines, animation, audio, pointer/input, runtime bridge and three.js rendering), `packages/editor` (React + Vite + Monaco browser editor; owns the project template), `packages/behaviors` (motors, roles, combat in both spaces, interaction, grid navigation/pathfinding, point-and-click, and since issue #181 the 3D `enemy` role, checkpoints and knockback), four archetypes (platformer, topdown, isometric and, since issue #181, `third-person`: an orbit camera, camera-relative controls and 3D melee in a CC0 KayKit dungeon courtyard), `packages/mcp`, `packages/cli`, the private lint toolchain `packages/lint` (ESLint 9 + `typescript-eslint` on a lint-only `typescript@6.0.3`, never published), the private render/spawn benchmark `packages/bench` (never published), one Vite example per archetype (`examples/third-person`, `@waica/example-third-person`, private, replaced the 3D smoke example `examples/smoke-3d` in issue #181: a synced copy of the third-person demo).

`packages/mcp` is a private stdio MCP server with 16 tools: eleven file-oriented creation/introspection/validation/scaffold/configuration tools (since issue #200, `configure_desktop` edits `game.json`'s `desktop` block) plus five browser-backed Run Session tools. `packages/mcp/src/known-archetypes.ts` is the single source of truth for the four archetypes it can bundle, resolve and scaffold; `scaffold_prefab` emits a 3D component set for a 3D archetype (issue #181). `packages/cli` publishes the plain `waica` binary as `@waica/cli`; it serves the editor and bundles the MCP server plus vendored published-shape copies of the six public libraries, and since issue #200 `waica export desktop` packages a Project as an unsigned Electron app per platform (`@electron/packager`, Electron pinned exactly in its `devDependencies`, the shell served over `app://`, Steamworks opt-in through `steamworks.js` 0.4.0; ADR 0032).

Tests use Vitest 5 + happy-dom from the repository root (3994 tests in 424 files, counted 2026-10-15 on the issue #200 stack's top layer after its review fixes); editor render tests use Testing Library under StrictMode. The current published version is 0.29.1 (`v0.29.1`, `origin/main` 8b1e20d; npm lists `@waica/cli`, `@waica/engine`, `@waica/behaviors` and `@waica/archetype-third-person` at 0.29.1, checked with `npm view` on 2026-10-14). Recent engine contracts include one-live-scene unload/swap, scene/session-scoped audio, deterministic 1/60 s simulation steps, frame-based Runtime Bridge stepping, spatial queries, collision layers/masks, `game.time` timers/tweens, entity-anchored UI pieces, the session-scoped asset loader (`game.assets`) and camera effects (`game.cameraEffects`: shake, fade, flash; fading Scene Transitions) and, in 3D scenes, a Rapier world (`@dimforge/rapier3d-deterministic-compat` 0.21.0, loaded on demand: `Collider`, `RigidBody`, sensors, a kinematic character controller, 3D `game.query`) and, since issue #166, an `Animator` that plays a `Model`'s glTF clips once per Simulation Step (the Clip Target seam a `StateMachine` plays through in both spaces, the `clip:end` trigger, `CharacterMotor.turnSpeed`, the `character` role) and, since issue #173, a host view camera (`CameraRig.setViewCamera`/`sceneCamera`), a public `raycastPick` with extra targets and `glbClipNames`, through which the editor edits 3D scenes (ADR 0030: the Editor Camera, picking, `TransformControls` gizmos, a grid, helpers and glb clip dropdowns) and, since issue #181, the Orbit Camera (ADR 0031: a perspective `camera` block that `follow`s an entity, turned by the locked mouse, orbit Actions and the wheel, pulled in front of walls, with perspective shake), `Mouse:Left`/`Mouse:Right` as Action sources with pointer lock, and the Runtime Bridge's `look`.

**Seven packages publish together at one version:** `@waica/cli` plus `@waica/engine`, `@waica/behaviors`, `@waica/archetype-platformer`, `@waica/archetype-topdown`, `@waica/archetype-isometric` and `@waica/archetype-third-person` (first shipped in 0.29.0; its npm page exists and `.claude/skills/publish/SKILL.md` §0 holds the bootstrap history). `@waica/editor` and `@waica/mcp` remain private but carry the same version because they ship inside the CLI. Lockstep and packed-package behavior are enforced by tests and `scripts/test-dist.mjs`.

| `packages/editor` (React 19 + Vite, `react-dom`) | `packages/editor/src` (`.tsx` en `src/editor/`, `src/editor/inspector/`, `src/home/` y `src/*.tsx`) | `packages/editor/src/styles.css` (bloque `:root` con la paleta propia: `--bg`, `--bg-panel`, `--accent`, `--ctx-prefab`, `--ctx-ui`, ...; una sola hoja de 2616 lineas) | — (sin UI kit propio; los componentes viven junto a cada feature) | — | — | con sistema |

Razon del Estado: el editor define una paleta propia como variables CSS (no es un default de scaffold), asi que cuenta como `con sistema` por tokens propios, aunque no tiene `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`, Storybook, bundle `design-sync/` ni proyecto de Claude Design. Los 4 examples (`examples/*`) y `packages/bench` no declaran `react-dom`/`next`/`react-native`/`expo`: no son superficies UI. `DESIGN.md` en la raiz es el documento de vision del producto (arquitectura/arquetipos), no un sistema de diseno de UI, y no cuenta.

## Ambientes
- **Local only.** There is no staging/prod service, Docker, `.env` file, database, queue or external API. `import.meta.env.DEV` is the only detected environment lookup and is supplied by Vite; it is not a secret or operator-provided variable.
- **Prerequisites:** `pnpm install` at the root and a compatible system Google Chrome/Chromium for `pnpm test:e2e` and the browser leg of `pnpm test:dist`. `playwright-core` downloads no browser. Discovery is the fixed macOS/Linux list in `scripts/runtime-e2e.mjs`; the 2026-10-14 refresh used `/usr/bin/google-chrome-stable` 150.0.7871.186 on Linux (Node v24.15.0); an earlier refresh used `/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome` 153.0.8010.54 on macOS. A fresh Git worktree needs its own `pnpm install` before verification.
- **Benchmark host:** `chichex-linux`, reached over SSH (`~/.ssh/config`, `BatchMode=yes`), runs `pnpm bench:remote` so the benchmark never loads the maintainer's Mac. As of 2026-10-01: Linux x86_64, 8 cores, 30 GB, Node v24.21.0, Google Chrome 150.0.7871.186 at `/usr/bin/google-chrome-stable`, pnpm 11.4.0 installed user-level in `~/.local/bin` (the global npm prefix needs root; the remote scripts add `~/.local/bin` to `PATH`). Chrome renders WebGL there with SwiftShader (software: `ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device (Subzero)…), SwiftShader driver)`, verified 2026-10-02), so its default frame times measure a CPU-rendered worst case. The host also has an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (driver 615.71.09): `pnpm bench:remote --gpu` reaches it through ANGLE on Vulkan (`ANGLE (NVIDIA, Vulkan 1.4.351 (NVIDIA NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti …), NVIDIA)`, verified 2026-10-02), where every scenario is within budget. Its results are the committed baselines; it is not a CI runner.
- **CI:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every pull request against `main` (`ubuntu-latest`, Node 22): `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:dist`, `pnpm test:e2e` (one parallel job per `--group`, the matrix guarded by `packages/mcp/src/runtime-e2e-groups.test.ts`) and `pnpm audit --audit-level high`, and since issue #200 the `test:desktop (<os>)` job on `ubuntu-latest`, `windows-latest` and `macos-latest` (each exports its own platform and runs `pnpm test:desktop --steam`, which also installs `steamworks.js` and loads its addon; Linux adds `--cross` and runs under `xvfb-run` with openbox; the Electron zips are cached by the pinned Electron version), which `verify` needs. A PR whose base is not `main` (an upper layer of a stack) runs none of it. `.github/workflows/publish.yml` runs only on release tags and performs typecheck, unit tests and published-shape verification before publishing. `.github/workflows/claude-review.yml` is an on-demand PR review workflow (`workflow_dispatch`). `.github/dependabot.yml` schedules weekly npm and GitHub Actions updates.
- **SDD artifacts:** `.sdd/project.md`, 17 tracked feature specs in `.sdd/specs/`, 26 tracked handoffs in `.sdd/grills/` and 31 ADRs in `docs/adr/` at `origin/main` 8b1e20d (counted with `git ls-files` on 2026-10-14), plus `CONTEXT.md` as the domain glossary. Newer specs are issue-hosted in their issue bodies (e.g. #69, #70, #76, #74).
- **Git:** default branch `main`; remote `origin` = `https://github.com/chichex/waica.git` (verified `git remote -v` 2026-10-14); `gh` authenticated as `chichex`. `/skill:sdd-run` can branch from the updated `origin/main`, push a feature branch and open a PR. Merged branches are normally deleted, and PRs land as merge commits rather than squashes.

## Verificacion autonoma
Ladder for this repository, from cheapest to strongest:
1. **Typecheck:** `pnpm typecheck` (~3s), across all 15 non-root workspace projects.
2. **Lint:** `pnpm lint` (~18s), ESLint with type-aware rules plus the SHOULD-warning ratchet.
3. **Unit/component tests:** `pnpm test` (~22s), currently 3994 deterministic tests in 424 files. This is the primary TDD seam for engine, behavior, editor and MCP contracts.
4. **Build:** `pnpm build` (~4s), including clean library declaration/JavaScript output, all browser bundles, MCP template bundling and CLI editor/MCP/library vendoring.
5. **Published package shape:** `pnpm test:dist` (~17s), proving source/dist parity, publish manifests, package exports, normal Node imports, packed CLI stdio behavior and a packed browser Runtime Session.
6. **Packaged desktop app:** `pnpm test:desktop` (~18s on this host; `--cross`, `--steam` ~44s), exporting two generated Projects with `waica export desktop` and driving the packaged Linux binaries with playwright-core's `_electron` (logical state only). It needs the network for the Electron zips.
7. **Scripted browser e2e:** `pnpm test:e2e` (~97s wall on this Linux host for the webgl2 leg including the build, 2026-10-14; ~171s on macOS with both Render Backend legs before issue #181's third-person leg), driving the checkout CLI and real Chrome through deterministic Runtime Session operations, projection, movement, collision, combat, audio, point-and-click, scene swapping, screenshots and cleanup, the third-person demo played (orbit camera, camera-relative walk, fight, roll, respawn), and the editor's 3D edit view in its own dev server with the real mouse. Host/browser integration can fail; a missing browser is red.
8. **Live editor/example smoke:** start the relevant Vite command, probe its printed URL, and use browser automation when visual/editor behavior is in scope. The examples expose `window.__waica.game` in DEV for logical-state inspection; the editor exposes `window.__waicaEditor` in DEV (`openMemoryProject`, `readText`, `viewportGame`).

**Not autonomously verifiable:** subjective game feel (movement, camera, animation, knockback/stun and audio mix), absolute visual/art orientation beyond deterministic screenshots/state, and any npm publication. Release tags, deploy-like external mutation and npm state always require a human.

## Limites
- Never publish to npm without explicit human confirmation. Pushing a `v*` tag is the live publication path; `pnpm release` refuses local publication.
- Never push directly to `main`; work on branches and finish in a PR.
- Never merge PRs autonomously: merge remains a human decision.
- Never delete or rewrite published Git history.
- Deploys, shared-data migrations and paid services are absent; if introduced, treat them as human-only by default.

## Politicas de generacion
Cinco politicas de la tecnologia activas (`lint-clean` agregada el 2026-09-28 por el grill de coding policies compliance) (elegidas el 2026-08-21 tras research de buenas practicas TS cruzado contra las convenciones medidas del repo). Cada gate corre sobre el DIFF del PR contra su base — nunca audita codigo preexistente — y fue verificado ejecutandolo contra el diff real del PR #46 (119 archivos): los cuatro en verde. Las genericas (tamaño de PR, dependencias nuevas, commits convencionales) fueron ofrecidas el 2026-08-06 y declinadas; coverage sigue no activable (sin tooling, ver `## Gaps`).

| Politica | Valor | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| higiene-ts-diff | prohibidos en lineas nuevas: `: any`/`as any`, `@ts-ignore`/`@ts-expect-error`, `export default` y `enum` (`as never` y las definite assignments `entity!:` son idioma del repo y quedan permitidos; `.d.ts` y `*.test.ts` exentos) | dos greps sobre `git diff --unified=0 <base>...HEAD -- 'packages/*/src/*.ts' 'examples/*/src/*.ts' ':(exclude)*.test.ts' ':(exclude)*.d.ts'` lineas `^+`: (a) escapes/enum/default-export con comentarios removidos (`sed 's://.*::'`), (b) directivas `@ts-*` sobre la linea cruda. 0 hits = pasa |
| tests-acompañan-src | todo package que agrega `.ts` nuevos bajo `packages/<p>/src/` debe agregar o modificar al menos un `.test.ts` en ese mismo package dentro del PR | script: por cada package con archivos `--diff-filter=A` no-test bajo `src/`, exigir algun `*.test.ts` en el diff de ese package |
| max-lineas-archivo | ningun archivo `.ts` o `.tsx` tocado supera 950 lineas fisicas (ratchet sobre el baseline medido 2026-08-21: el mayor `.ts` es `packages/mcp/src/validation.ts` con 903; extendido a `.tsx` el 2026-09-28) | script: `wc -l` sobre cada `.ts`/`.tsx` del diff, tope 950 |
| lint-clean | `pnpm lint` termina en 0: ningun error de ESLint (reglas MUST de `.sdd/coding-policies.md`) y ninguna regresion del ratchet de warnings SHOULD (`packages/lint/lint-baseline.json`) | `pnpm lint` exit 0 |
| naming-archivos | archivos nuevos bajo `src/`: `.ts` en kebab-case; `.tsx` en PascalCase o kebab-case (convencion React del editor) | grep del basename de cada archivo `--diff-filter=A` contra `^([a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*\.(ts|json|html|png|md|glb|gltf)|([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*|[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*)\.tsx)$` |
| diseño-hex-editor | no superar el baseline (100, 2026-10-14) de colores hex en `.tsx` del editor fuera de los tokens de `packages/editor/src/styles.css` | `git grep -IhoE '#([0-9a-fA-F]{3}){1,2}' -- 'packages/editor/src/**/*.tsx' ':!packages/editor/src/styles.css' \| wc -l` <= 100 |
| diseño-inline-editor | no superar el baseline (3, 2026-10-14) de estilos inline `style={{` en `.tsx` del editor (no hay UI kit que excluir) | `git grep -h 'style={{' -- 'packages/editor/src/**/*.tsx' \| wc -l` <= 3 |
| coding-policies | .sdd/coding-policies.md (typescript, react, node) | guia — sin gate: /sdd-run la sigue al generar, la juzga el reviewer |

## Gaps
- PR CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the ladder through `pnpm test:e2e` plus `pnpm audit --audit-level high` on every PR against `main`. It is not yet a required status check in the branch protection settings; making it required is a repository-settings decision for a human.
- `[NEEDS-INPUT]` No coverage tooling is configured; there is no verified coverage command or measured baseline, so a coverage generation policy is not activable.
- `[NEEDS-INPUT]` Browser gates depend on a host-installed Chrome/Chromium selected from a fixed candidate list. Release runs through `v0.19.0` (the last one this section recorded) have succeeded on `ubuntu-latest`, but the runner browser is not explicitly pinned.
- `pnpm release` is intentionally untested because release tags publish externally.
- Vite reports informational >500 kB chunk warnings for the editor and examples; code-splitting remains future work.
- `pnpm test:e2e`'s webgpu leg fails on the Linux host `chichex` (Chrome 150, `--enable-unsafe-webgpu`): the topdown leg reads 0 -> 0.188 for a 30-frame walk, identically at `origin/main` aa14fc1 and again on 2026-10-14 at 8b1e20d, and a plain three page there fails `createBuffer` on its first frame, so no later leg (third-person, editor-3d) runs on it there. CI's `ubuntu-latest` passed both legs at aa14fc1 (not re-checked on 2026-10-14). Verifying the webgpu leg needs CI or macOS.
